title: Lithuania - national associations history page
supported_statement: REUSE; SHA re-verified. UEFA's official history states the LFF was readmitted to FIFA on 9 December 1991 and became a full UEFA member at the 1992 Congress in Gothenburg.
limitations: Confederation account; conflicts with both the FIFA report year 1992 and the UPI report of the 3 July 1992 Congress acceptance; whether 'readmission' refers to an ExCo decision later confirmed by Congress is not established.

title: South Africa readmitted to FIFA
locator: Full article (read online via fetch tool)
supported_statement: Contemporaneous wire report dated Zurich, 3 July 1992: at the FIFA Congress that Friday (3 July 1992) 14 nations were accepted as members; the article names Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Russia, Armenia, Belarus, Georgia, Ukraine, South Africa, Croatia, Slovenia, St. Kitts and Nevis (12 of the 14; South Africa named twice). It states the three Baltic states had previously been FIFA members until 1940. It further states applications from other national associations were postponed and the Congress left it to the Executive Committee to decide at a December meeting whether Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kirghizia (Kyrgyzstan), Moldova, Uzbekistan, Tadzhikistan (Tajikistan) and Turkmenistan should be granted membership. After the additions FIFA had 178 members.
limitations: Local copy could not be saved: direct download from upi.com is unreachable from this network (curl exit 7 on repeated attempts); the full text was read online through the platform fetch tool. Wire report of the Congress, not a FIFA document; the two unnamed members of the 14 are not identified in this source.

publisher: Los Angeles Times (staff and wire reports)
title: Soccer - South Africa readmitted; full list of 14 associations admitted at the FIFA Congress
supported_statement: Contemporaneous report dated 4 July 1992: South Africa readmitted after a 29-year ban; FIFA also admitted Armenia, Belarus, Georgia, Russia and Ukraine from the former Soviet Union; the former Yugoslav republics of Croatia and Slovenia; the Cayman Islands, Namibia and St. Kitts-Nevis; and 'The Baltic republics of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, granted provisional membership in December, also were admitted.'
limitations: Wire report, not a FIFA document. It completes the 14 admitted at the 3 July 1992 Congress (UPI named 12; this names the other two: Cayman Islands and Namibia) and documents that the Baltic states held provisional FIFA membership from December (1991, matching UEFA's 9 December 1991 readmission date) before full admission at the Congress. No FIFA primary obtained for any of these events.
